name: Muhlenbergia

flags: muhlenbergia-piniflora — provisional source-concept learner; the source name appears erroneous and the species package must remain visibly flagged until provenance is corrected.
project_scope.note: This genus module preserves all current canonical project concepts but does not treat the flagged M. piniflora source name as a secure teaching anchor.

recognition.where_to_look_first: The project set spans large fountain-form bunchgrasses, small tight bunchgrasses, creeping nimblewill, and rhizomatous low muhly. Start with growth form and scale, then inspect the ligule, leaf folding/rolling, and panicle size and openness.
priority: upright bunchgrass versus creeping/rooting or rhizomatous habit
flat versus folded or involute blades
open feathery versus narrow contracted panicle
spikelet size and awn detail when the habit split is not enough

quick_split: M. lindheimeri — large upright fountain-form bunchgrass with unusually long membranous ligules and a tall feathery panicle.
M. reverchonii — smaller compact bunchgrass with threadlike involute leaves and a delicate open reddish panicle.
M. schreberi — low weak creeping grass that roots at lower nodes; narrow contracted panicle.
M. utilis — short rhizomatous grass with creeping scaly rhizomes, filiform involute leaves, and a small narrow panicle.
M. ×involuta — dense upright bunchgrass with firm folded leaves and morphology intermediate between Lindheimer and seep muhly.
M. piniflora — keep visibly provisional; do not use as a final visual key until the source-name problem is resolved.
comparison_lesson.nursery_warning: Do not use pink plume color by itself to call a plant M. lindheimeri. The widely sold M. capillaris concept is not a project-native Central Texas anchor.
